candidates.title: Epic: Unified Verification and Failure Intelligence in Cezar Factory
candidates.body:
<!-- unified-verification-2026-10-23:epic -->
## Objective
Deliver a backward-compatible, project-agnostic unified Verification capability inside Cezar Factory, with focused testing, nonblocking known-debt policy, persistent recurrence history and optional Hindsight contextual recall. TableFlux (blackjackandhookersGodot) is the pilot, not a hardcoded runtime dependency.

## Architecture draft
[Draft design (planning branch)](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/planning/unified-verification-2026-10-23/docs/unified-verification-draft-2026-10-23.md)

## Existing related work — do not duplicate
- #19 explicit project-owned validation adapters and #39 target migration are prerequisites for backward compatibility.
- #22, #30, #31 bounded collector and canonical GitHub publisher stay authoritative for their respective Factory failure-audit flow. Integrate, do not replace.
- #17 reliability audit and release gating remain independently applicable.

## Decisions
- Reuse current scheduler/workflow system; Verification is a typed execution plus results and policy layer.
- Project-owned test implementations run standalone; no GdUnit or Gua reimplementation in Factory.
- Normalized findings in a deterministic Cezar ledger; Hindsight only as advisory project-scoped memory, never source of truth.
- Focused test selection explained by impact evidence, plus periodic wider coverage.
- Existing known failures do not automatically block unrelated agent work. New/worsened regressions and incomplete coverage remain visible; stricter merge/release gates unaffected.
- Gua remains optional and deferred until isolated evaluation passes.

## Tracking and acceptance
- [ ] Contract, adapters and isolation usable on Windows/Linux with fixture-driven negative tests.
- [ ] Focused TableFlux verification uses Git diff + ownership/dependencies, with selection reasons.
- [ ] Failure episodes and comparisons correctly classify existing/new/worsening/resolved/reopened/untested/infra results.
- [ ] Hindsight offline leaves deterministic verification available.
- [ ] Compact agent summaries, artifacts, UI/CLI and safe agent loops.
- [ ] Independent review, risk approvals and release through explicitly registered targets; no deployment from this planning issue.

## Dependencies and governance
See individual child issues for implementation acceptance criteria and sequencing. Plan is drafted, not a high-risk implementation approval. Read AGENTS.md, policies/risk.yaml, policies/definition-of-ready.md, docs/project-integration.md, #19, #22 and associated children. Do not place private TableFlux issue evidence or host paths into this public repository.

**Risk:** high (cross-project quality gates and agent automation); **complexity:** high. Keep implementation blocked pending policy-required plan approval and prerequisite reconciliation.


## Work packages and sequence
- [ ] #48 — Existing context: #19, #39, #22, #30, #31. Can begin immediately.
- [ ] #49 — Requires #48; coordinate schema migration with #19 and #39.
- [ ] #50 — Requires #49 and compatibility with #19.
- [ ] #51 — Requires #50; coordinate project adapter migration with #39.
- [ ] #52 — Requires #49 and #50; coexist with #22/#30/#31, no duplicate publication.
- [ ] #53 — Requires #49, #51; consumes finding evidence from #52 when available.
- [ ] #54 — Requires #52 and #53, using comparison result contracts from #49.
- [ ] #55 — Requires #52; follows redaction and collection constraints of #30; optional to all core execution.
- [ ] #56 — Requires #53 and #54, plus #52 evidence. #55 is optional. Coordinate GitHub publishing with #31.
- [ ] #57 — Requires #50, #52, #53 and #54.
- [ ] #58 — Requires #50, #51 and #54; Gua adapter requires passing isolated Gua evaluation.
- [ ] #59 — Requires #50, #54 and #57; remote worker rollout after local pilot.

### Delivery lanes
Foundation: #48 → #49 → #50 → #51. Findings and impact: #52 → #53 → #54. Optional memory: #52 → #55. Agent + UX: #54 → #56 and #57. Advanced: #58 and #59. Contract/adapter work must respect #19/#39; failure publication respects #22/#30/#31.

No issue is automatically approved for implementation solely by this plan.

candidates.title: Define versioned verification, result and compatibility contracts
candidates.body:
## Objective
Define the shared execution/check/result schema *before* implementation while keeping existing `validation.changed/full/verify` functional (#19).

## Work
- [ ] Define manifest opt-in extension, schema versioning/migration, optional capabilities, explicit no-tests/skipped/unknown statuses.
- [ ] Define run/check/test result, diagnostics, metrics, coverage, fingerprint, environment, provenance, artifact references and bounds.
- [ ] Specify result aggregation, semantic exit codes, cancellations, timeouts, crash and truncated/partial evidence handling.
- [ ] Clarify that performance policy consumes existing metrics; Cezar artifacts are distinct from #30's failure-audit evidence.
- [ ] Include valid and malformed fixtures, schema docs and independent test implementation requirements.

## Acceptance
Existing project adapters remain valid; zero tests, parse failures, unknown schema and tool crash never green; Windows/Linux contract tests demonstrate compatibility. Dependency: audit child and #19; risk high (cross-project contract), complexity medium.

## Governance
Parent: #47. Design: [Unified Verification draft](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/planning/unified-verification-2026-10-23/docs/unified-verification-draft-2026-10-23.md). Required reading: AGENTS.md, policies/risk.yaml, policies/definition-of-ready.md and docs/project-integration.md. Planning-only issue; comply with risk-based approval, reviewed dev PR, full Factory verification and explicitly registered target release. Never deploy as a side effect of tests.

## Sequencing and related issues
Requires #48; coordinate schema migration with #19 and #39.
Tracking epic: #47. Related work must not be duplicated.

## Linked dependencies
Depends on #48 and compatibility with #19/#39.
Parent epic: #47.

candidates.title: Implement isolated generic verification executor and adapter protocol
candidates.body:
## Objective
Reusable runner invoking project-owned tools through Cezar's existing scheduler, not replacing it.

## Work
- [ ] Implement preflight, execute, collect and cleanup extension points, optional discovery, cancellation, timeout and resource requirements.
- [ ] Enforce explicit project registry/worktree, worktree-local unique artifacts, redaction and bounded logs.
- [ ] Normalize exit status and infrastructure failure separately from test failure, including no-tests.
- [ ] Capture immutable run identity, environment/tool/commit provenance and execution trace.
- [ ] Add fault-injection fixtures for hanging/crashed commands, missing executables, concurrent worktrees, spaces in paths and bad output.

## Acceptance
Two concurrent runs have isolated artifacts, cancellation terminates child process tree, no false positives, runs local Windows/Linux; existing #19 adapters remain supported. Dependencies: contract, #19. Risk high; complexity high.

## Governance
Parent: #47. Design: [Unified Verification draft](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/planning/unified-verification-2026-10-23/docs/unified-verification-draft-2026-10-23.md). Required reading: AGENTS.md, policies/risk.yaml, policies/definition-of-ready.md and docs/project-integration.md. Planning-only issue; comply with risk-based approval, reviewed dev PR, full Factory verification and explicitly registered target release. Never deploy as a side effect of tests.

## Sequencing and related issues
Requires #49 and compatibility with #19.
Tracking epic: #47. Related work must not be duplicated.

## Linked dependencies
Depends on #49; integrates with #19 rather than replacing it.
